definition: Canonicalizing Arabic spelling variation before processing: hamza forms (أ إ آ ا), ta marbuta vs.
details: Canonicalizing Arabic spelling variation before processing: hamza forms (أ إ آ ا), ta marbuta vs. ha (ة / ه), alef maqsura vs. ya (ى / ي), removing tatweel (ـــ) and optional diacritics. Small preprocessing decisions here move retrieval and matching metrics more than model choice sometimes does; the normalization scheme must be identical at indexing and query time.

explainer.lead: Orthographic normalization canonicalizes Arabic spelling variation before processing. It matters because these small preprocessing decisions can move retrieval and matching metrics more than model choice sometimes does.

tiers.eli5: It tidies up different ways of writing the same word so a search treats them all as one.
tiers.practitioner: It canonicalizes hamza forms (أ إ آ ا), ta marbuta versus ha (ة / ه), alef maqsura versus ya (ى / ي), and removes tatweel (ـــ) and optional diacritics. A pitfall is that the normalization scheme must be identical at indexing and query time.
tiers.paperLevel: A preprocessing step canonicalizing Arabic spelling variation: hamza forms, ta marbuta vs ha, alef maqsura vs ya, removal of tatweel and optional diacritics, with the scheme required to be identical at indexing and query time.

explainer.example: A query written with a hamza form is normalized to match documents indexed with the plain alef form, so retrieval succeeds.
